patch.value: GH-1774: parity review findings: cmd.exe-unsafe recovery commands, a claim with unreadable history reported as active, and a release after a force-claim clears the replacement holder

GH-1774 (filed 2026-11-23 from the pm-rust parity review; the Rust port reproduces each byte for byte and waits for pm-cli's decision). (1) A Windows recovery command for a tracker path containing %TRACKER% (pm --pm-path "C:\repo\%TRACKER%\pm" get item-1) is not safe to paste into cmd.exe, which expands %VAR% inside double quotes, so a pasted recovery can target another tracker; expected: escape % for cmd.exe or state that the command is for PowerShell only. pm-kjoudp (open) owns the PowerShell side of the same paste-safety contract. (2) Claiming an item whose holder's history is unreadable reports the holder as 'active under mutation_guard.stale_in_progress_hours=72' although activity could not be judged; expected: a distinct activity-unknown holder state. (3) After close, a force-claim by a second holder, then a release by the original holder clears the replacement holder (warn policy, with ownership_warning:assignee_conflict; strict policy with --force); expected: a release that ends a close releases only the holder that close ended. Duplicate check: searched cmd.exe recovery percent expansion, claim unreadable history activity unknown, release after force claim replacement holder; only pm-kjoudp overlaps (PowerShell quoting).

Windows recovery commands are paste-safe in cmd.exe (percent expansion neutralized) or explicitly declared PowerShell-only, with a rendering test for a %VAR% path; A holder whose activity cannot be judged is reported with a distinct activity-unknown state in claim refusals; Releasing as the holder a close ended never clears a replacement holder under either ownership policy
Recovery commands, holder activity and release ownership each behave as the parity review expects
